note: Frozen BEFORE candidate testing. The launch decision recomputes eligibility from this file plus validated measurements; nothing in an evidence manifest may select its own requirements. Changing any value here is a product decision that invalidates every receipt collected under the previous hash.

scope.decision: Version 2 NARROWS the advertised promise to what can be proven, rather than keeping a promise the evidence does not reach. This is a deliberate product decision, taken on 2026-09-09 with the operator's authorization, and it is why the policy hash changed: every receipt gathered under version 1 is void and was recollected.
scope.certified: Claude Code on macOS (darwin), with a vendor runtime receipt for the exact candidate package.
scope.preview: Copilot, Cursor, Codex, Windsurf, Gemini and VS Code on any platform, and every client on native Linux and Windows. These are wired, protocol-tested and documented, but carry NO vendor runtime evidence, so they must be described as preview/uncertified in every public artifact — never as supported.
scope.crossDeviceSync: preview only; production promotion requires a separate decision and scope authorization.
scope.publication: A GO from this policy approves THE CANDIDATE against the narrowed promise. Publishing additionally requires the tag workflow's aggregate over every osNodeCell below, which runs on real CI runners.

uncertified.meaning: Listed here so the narrowing is explicit in the artifact rather than implied by an absence. Moving any of these into `clients`/`clientPlatforms` restores its cell as a hard requirement and changes this hash.

freshness.failureTreatment: a missed transition or a timeout counts as a failed sample, never as a discarded one
freshness.configuration: production defaults — no shortened fallback, no overridden debounce
freshness.clock: from the source mutation to the moment every reader agrees — not to a capture or bookkeeping event
